Repo: /opt/nxeon (Next.js/TypeScript/Prisma/Postgres — Nxeon hosting platform), a real git repo. Standing rule: NEVER build/run dev servers/run `npm run build` in the live prod tree `/opt/nxeon` or the shared staging tree `/opt/nxeon-staging` — a past agent clobbering `.next` there broke production. Start by creating your own isolated worktree:
```
cd /opt/nxeon && git worktree add /opt/nxeon-wip-about-page -b feature/about-page-founder-story
cd /opt/nxeon-wip-about-page && npm install
```
Do ALL reading, editing, building, and testing inside `/opt/nxeon-wip-about-page` from that point on.

GOAL: completely recreate Nxeon's About page (find it under `app/(marketing)/` — likely `app/(marketing)/about/page.tsx`, confirm the exact path first) to be far more personable, telling the real founding story instead of whatever generic/corporate copy is there now. This is a full creative rewrite AND a full technical restructuring of the page, not a copy tweak.

## The story (owner's own words — fill in the blanks and invent believable, specific, warm details; don't leave anything generic or hand-wavy)

Three brothers left the 9-to-5 grind in Canada to travel. They eventually landed in Vietnam (Da Nang specifically — see the photo below, taken with the Dragon Bridge / Cầu Rồng visible in the background, a real, recognizable Da Nang landmark) while building a website together and needed a server. They picked one up from an ordinary host, only to get hit with a much higher price at renewal than what they signed up for — the classic bait-and-switch "teaser price, quietly-hiked renewal" trick. Tired of that pattern across the hosting industry generally (not just one host — "a bunch of different hosting companies" use it), they decided to build the hosting company they wished existed. "Built with love in Vietnam."

Use this to inform (don't just restate) the actual "why" behind Nxeon's own well-established real product decisions already in this codebase — the story should connect authentically to features that ALREADY EXIST, not invent aspirational ones:
- The platform's actual headline pricing promise, verbatim, is: "The price you sign up at is the price you renew at — it never increases at renewal." (see `components/marketing/PricingExplorer.tsx`'s hero copy: "Lock in your price today.") — this is literally the product decision that grew directly out of the exact renewal-price-hike experience in the story. Make this connection explicit and central, not a coincidence.
- Real, live products to ground the story in specifics rather than vague "we host websites": Cloud VPS, Game Servers, Shared Hosting, Business Email, Domains (see `components/marketing/PricingExplorer.tsx`'s `PRODUCTS` array for the exact current lineup).
- The company is genuinely based in / operates out of Vietnam — the infrastructure itself is real (a Singapore datacenter for low-latency APAC — see other marketing pages' "Singapore data center · Low-latency APAC" copy), so "Built with love in Vietnam" should read as the founders' home base / where the company was actually started, while the actual server infrastructure being Singapore-based (for real latency reasons) is a separate, compatible fact — don't conflate "built in Vietnam" with "hosted in Vietnam," keep both true and distinct.

Invent specific, human, plausible details to fill gaps — approximate founding year consistent with `© 2026 Nxeon` copyright notices already in the codebase footer (so the company reads as a few years old, not brand new, unless other evidence says otherwise — check the footer/copyright year and any other dated references in the codebase for consistency), the brothers' rough roles (e.g., one more technical/infrastructure-focused, one more product/design-focused, one more business/customer-facing — make it feel real and differentiated, not three interchangeable people), what the original website project was (something believable a small team building "for a couple of guys traveling" would actually build — don't overthink it, a simple concrete detail beats a vague one), and the specific moment/feeling of getting that renewal invoice. Keep it warm, honest, a little self-deprecating about being naive first-time customers themselves — NOT corporate-mission-statement voice. Do not fabricate specific dollar amounts, named competitor hosts, or verifiable claims (like specific years/cities beyond Da Nang/Vietnam/Canada, or invented review counts/customer numbers) that could read as false advertising — invented FEEL and color is good, invented VERIFIABLE FACTS are not.

## The photo

A real photo of the three brothers, at night, on a rooftop overlooking Da Nang's Dragon Bridge (visible lit up gold in the background), dressed casually (linen shirts), smiling, arms around each other. It currently lives at:
`/opt/nxeon/board-uploads/board/cmtehxr35003ghlq5239wl32d/5c7857d861c91262dc12c5a0.png`
Copy it into this worktree's `public/` directory (e.g. `public/about/founders-danang.jpg` or similar — reprocess/optimize it if this codebase has an established image-optimization convention for marketing photos elsewhere, check for one before deciding) and use it as a genuine hero/centerpiece image on the new About page — not a small throwaway thumbnail. Look at how other marketing pages in this codebase (e.g. `components/marketing/GameLogo.tsx`'s real-photo patterns, or any existing team/photo usage) handle real photography for visual/technical conventions to match (Next.js `<Image>` usage, aspect ratio handling, etc.).

## Technical scope

This is a "complete restructuring," per the owner — don't just edit copy in the existing page structure if the existing structure doesn't serve a personal story well. Look at how this codebase's OTHER marketing pages are built (the homepage `app/page.tsx`, `app/(marketing)/game-servers/page.tsx`, etc.) for the established visual language (navy/violet/cyan brand theme — see any existing design-system references/tokens in `app/globals.css` or `tailwind.config`), component patterns (`Reveal` for scroll-in animation, `.rail` for the content-width wrapper, card/section conventions), and reuse them — this must look like it belongs on Nxeon, not like a generic templated "about us" page. Structure suggestion (adapt as the story and photo dictate, don't treat this as rigid): a personal, first-person-plural opening hook (not "Welcome to Nxeon" boilerplate) → the Da Nang photo as a real visual anchor early on → the renewal-price-hike moment as the turning point → how that directly produced the "price you sign up at is the price you renew at" promise → what Nxeon actually is today (grounded in the real product lineup) → a warm, human sign-off (not "Our mission is...").

## Standing rules for this repo (non-negotiable)

- No schema changes needed for this task; if you find yourself wanting one, stop and flag it instead.
- Never rotate/touch any live credential.
- Match the codebase's comment style: comments explain non-obvious WHY, not WHAT. Don't over-comment new prose/JSX.
- Don't fabricate real-sounding but false verifiable claims (see above) — warmth and specificity in FEEL is good, invented facts presented as true are not.

## Verification (required before reporting done)

1. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
2. Full test suite (`npm test`), diffed by exact failing-test-name against a fresh run on `main` in the same worktree — zero NEW failures.
3. Visual verification: get the page rendering (local dev server or build) and take a Playwright screenshot (desktop and mobile viewport) — confirm the photo actually renders, isn't broken/oversized/cropped oddly, and the page reads as a coherent, on-brand redesign rather than a broken layout. Include the screenshots' file paths in your report.
4. Commit your work on the `feature/about-page-founder-story` branch inside the worktree (do not push, do not merge to main, do not deploy anywhere).

Report back with: the final page copy (or a clear summary of it), the exact files changed/added, where the photo ended up and how it's used, confirmation of tsc/test/visual results, and any creative choices you made that the owner might want to weigh in on (e.g. exact founding year invented, the invented website-building project detail, role differentiation between the three brothers).
